agenda_text:
CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR MARCH 7, 2022 AT 4:00 P.M. WILL TAKE PLACE
SOLELY BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
City
Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of
the public may provide live public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to
the start of public comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item, please
indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker Card Help Line : If
a public comment speaker needs assistance in completing a speaker card, please
call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124. Help line will open
30 minutes prior to the posted
start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the
published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone.
The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the
virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.
Your phone call to the City Council
meeting will be recorded as part of the City Council meeting. By
staying on the line and making public comment during the City Council meeting,
you are agreeing to have your phone call recorded.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may
submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of the meeting, at the
following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council
prior to the start of the meeting, posted online, and made part of the
legislative record for the item.
LIVESTREAM WITH CAPTIONING IS AVAILABLE AT
WWW.PASADENAMEDIA.ORG ,
AND ALSO AT
WWW.CITYOFPASADENA.NET/COMMISSIONS/AGENDAS ,
TO
HEAR A LIVE SPANISH TRANSLATION OF THE MEETING (LISTEN ONLY), PLEASE DIAL-IN 10
MINUTES PRIOR TO THE MEETING (3:50 P.M.):
TOLL-FREE DIAL-IN: (888) 585-9008
PARTICIPANT PASSCODE: 739-142-091, THEN #
IF YOU NEED A REASONABLE MODIFICATION OR ACCOMMODATION PURSUANT TO THE AMERICANS
WITH DISABILITIES ACT
BECAUSE YOU ARE UNABLE TO PARTICIPATE
ELECTRONICALLY AS SET FORTH ABOVE, CONTACT THE CITY CLERK’S OFFICE
AS SOON AS POSSIBLE AT (626) 744-4124 OR
CITYCLERK@CITYOFPASADENA.NET .
____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
LA REUNIÓN ESPECIAL DEL CONSEJO MUNICIPAL DEL 7 DE MARZO DE 2022 A LAS 4:00 P.M.
TENDRÁ LUGAR ÚNICAMENTE POR VIDEOCONFERENCIA/TELECONFERENCIA.
City
Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
Para facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente
por medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la
siguiente manera:
1. Durante la reunión, los miembros del
público pueden hacer comentarios públicos en vivo presentando una tarjeta de
oratoria antes del inicio del comentario sobre el artículo que se está tratando
en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los
oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado en la
agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo
Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el
Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2. Línea
de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pública :
Si un orador de comentario público
necesita asistencia para completar su tarjeta, puede llamar
a la Oficina del
Secretario de la Ciudad al
(626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda abrirá 30
minutos antes del inicio de la reunión.
Después de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pública, únase a la reunión virtual
a la hora de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro dispositivo electrónico
o por
teléfono. Debe usar el
mismo nombre o número de teléfono de la tarjeta de oratoria para la reunión
virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
orador.
Su llamada telefónica a la reunión del Concejo
Municipal se grabará como parte de la
reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al permanecer en la línea y hacer
comentarios públicos durante la
reunión del Concejo Municipal, está aceptando que se grabe su llamada
telefónica.
Computadoras y dispositivos electrónicos pueden sumarse a la reunión en:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Número para ingresar a la reunión por teléfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
reunión: 161 482 446
3. Los miembros del público
pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier longitud antes del inicio de
la reunión a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La
correspondencia se enviará al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de la reunión,
se publicará en línea, y se incorporará al registro legislativo sobre el
artículo.

minutes_text:
CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 7, 2022 - 4:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

  The meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo and President Pomeroy called the Special Joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Unified School
  District (PUSD) Board of Education to order at 4:06 p.m. The
  Pledge of Allegiance was led by PUSD President Pomeroy.

ROLL CALL:
 Councilmembers:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  Interim City Manager Cynthia Kurtz
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

Pasadena Unified School  President Elizabeth Pomeroy
District, Board of Education  Vice President Michelle Richardson Bailey
  Boardmember Kimberly Kenne
  Boardmember Jennifer Hall Lee
  Boardmember Patrick Cahalan
  Boardmember Tina Fredericks
  Boardmember Scott Phelps (Absent)

  Staff:  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools
  Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Chief Academic Officer
  Leslie Barnes, Ed.D., Chief Business Officer
  Ree A. Harris-Hudson, Director of Early Childhood Education
  Department

  HIGHLIGHT OF PUSD PROGRAMS PRESENTED BY PUSD

  Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Chief Academic Officer, and Ree A.
  Harris-Hudson, Director of Early Childhood Education
  Department, jointly presented a PowerPoint presentation on
  many of the Pasadena Unified School District's (PUSD)
  programs, and responded to questions.

Council Minutes  03/07/2022
   Boardmember Kenne provided information on PUSD's
Councilmembers Rivas and  International Baccalaureate Programmes and Math Academies.
Madison connected to the  Boardmember  Cahalan  and  Dr.  Brian  McDonald,
meeting at 4:11 p.m., and  Superintendent of Schools, provided information on PUSD's
4:14 p.m., respectively.  Center for Independent Study (CIS) Academy student
  enrollment numbers and program purpose. Boardmember Hall
  Lee provided information on Blair High School's Junior Reserve
  Officers Training Corp (JROTC) program.

  President Elizabeth Pomeroy encouraged Councilmembers to
  participate in the School District's Principal for a Day program,
  sponsored by Pasadena Educational Foundation (PEF) to get a
  better understanding of programs occurring at PUSD's schools.

  Councilmember Hampton asked PUSD staff to provide
  information on PUSD's most popular programs; and
  recommended that Board of Education and City Council focus
  on and support successful student programs that garner the
  most interest of Pasadena students.

  Ms. Blanco responded that PUSD staff is currently working on a
  Return on Investment project that will analyze all PUSD's
  initiatives and programs. and will share the data with the City
  Council once the project is complete.  In response to
  Councilmember Hampton's request, Ms. Blanco stated that
  PUSD staff will also provide data on the number of students who
  are graduating from John Muir High School with college credits.

  Following discussion, Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that
  one letter expressing concerns with PUSD not recognizing Blair
  High School's JROTC program, was received by the City Clerk's
  Office, distributed to the City Council and Board of Education,
  posted online, and made part of the public record for the item.

  Gabriel Lizardo, Pasadena resident, advocated for Latino
  representation on the Pasadena Unified School District
  Board; and expressed concerns with Latino student's
  reading capabilities and graduation rates.

  In response to the public speaker and comments from
  Councilmember Kennedy, Dr. McDonald stated that he will
  contact the public speaker to discuss and address his concerns
  related to student reading abilities and graduation rates of Latino
  students from PUSD.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed .

Council Minutes  2  03/07/2022
   COMMUNITY SAFETY INTERVENTION PROGRAMS FOR
  YOUTH PRESENTED BY CITY OF PASADENA

  Brenda Harvey Williams, Interim Assistant City Manager,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and
  responded to questions.

  Boardmember Fredericks advocated for joint, collaborative and
  integrated programs addressing student and community safety
  between PUSD and the City.

  Interim City Manager Kurtz stated her willingness to meet with
  PUSD representatives to review both agencies' programs to
  determine if greater collaboration might occur for a larger
  community impact; and responded to questions.

  Mayor Gordo responded that representatives from both PUSD
  and the City will meet to discuss Measures I and J, which will be
  a good opportunity to discuss collaborative community and
  school programs.

  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools, provided
  information on PUSD's internship school programs for PUSD
  students; and responded to questions

  Councilmember Kennedy advocated for PUSD to consider
  implementing a paid internship program similar to the City's
  Realizing Opportunities through Summer Employment (ROSE)
  program for PUSD students as another way to provide them with
  job training and monetary stipends.

  Ricky Pickens, Community Violence Interventionist, provided
  information on the changing dynamics of gang intervention; and
  responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that three letters providing
  comments on the matter, were received by the City Clerk's
  Office, distributed to the City Council and Board of Education,
  posted on line, and made part of the public record for the item.

  The following individuals provided comments on the matter:

  Michael Williams, Pasadena resident
  Brittney Pollock, Sherman Oaks resident
  Julia R., Los Angeles resident
  Christy Zamani, representing Day One
  Colin Bogart, representing Day One
  Carolyn Ghiloni, Sierra Madre resident
  Daniel Fong, representing Day One

Council Minutes  3  03/07/2022
   Yadi, Pasadena resident
  Julie Martinez, Pasadena resident
  Hiram Cormier Jr., Los Angeles resident
  Kareena K., representing Black Lives Matter - Los Angeles
  Kate Mcinerny, Pasadena resident
  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed .

  CURRENT JOINT USE AGREEMENTS PRESENTED BY
  PUSD
  Leslie Barnes, Ed.D. Chief Business Officer, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item, including information on
  the various joint use agreement amendments; and responded to
  questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson provided information on the signed
  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for McKinley School
  which will provide both tennis and pickleball courts for the
  community.

  Councilmember Williams requested information on the viability
  and process for converting closed PUSD schools into open
  space or creating additional MOU's for recreational uses, which
  may require amending the priority use order.  She also
  advocated for open recreational hours at PUSD school sites to
  allow pickle ball players some priority.

  Council member Hampton asked staff to review PUS D's joint use
  agreements to ensure PUSD students are not displaced in favor
  of allowing outside organizations priority use of PUSD
  recreational spaces and facilities.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that twenty letters advocating
  for additional shared facilities within PUS□ schools to allow for
  the playing of pickleball, and four letters advocating for additional
  open park space, were received by the City Clerk's Office,
  distributed to the City Council and Board of Education, posted
  online, and made part of the public record for the item.

  The following individuals provided comments on the matter:

  Mike Alvidrez, representing Pickleball Players of Pasadena
  Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community
  Happen
  Christy Zamani, representing Partnership for Children,
  Youth, and Families

Council Minutes  4  03/07/2022
   Interim City Manager Kurtz provided information on American
  Youth Soccer Organization (AYSO), Tom Sawyer Camps, and
  iTennis Rose Bowl lease agreements that use City properties;
  and responded to questions.

  Boardmember Cahalan, member of PUSD's Facilities
  Committee, invited the City Council to attend a Committee
  meeting to discuss various issues, including workforce housing.

  Mayor Gordo suggested that a City staff member be assigned to
  attend PUSD's Facilities Committee meetings as a way to track
  the discussion on matters relevant to the City and collaboration
  with the School District. He also spoke on the need to for the
  City Council, PUSD Board of Education, and Pasadena City
  College (PCC) Board of Trustees to meet and discuss broader
  aspects of education in Pasadena, including educational needs,
  land use consistency, and vacant (or soon to be vacant)
  properties.

  Councilmember  Kennedy  suggested  that  PUSD's
  representatives contact Mr. Jim Osterling, PCC Trustee, who is
  involved in creating workforce housing.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  CITY COUNCIL'S TASK FORCE ON EARLY CHILDHOOD
  DEVELOPMENT AND EARLY LEARNING PRESENTED BY
  CITY OF PASADENA

  Interim City Manager Kurtz, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the item, including information on the
  establishment of a new Task Force and its work plan; and
  responded to questions. Mayor Gordo spoke on the importance
  of early childhood education to prepare children for when they
  enter into PUSD's education system.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that one letter thanking the City
  Council for considering early childhood education, and
  advocating for a smarter approach to crime prevention within
  school age children in PUSD schools, was received by the City
  Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council and Board of
  Education, posted online, and made part of the public record for
  the item.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed .

Council Minutes  5  03/07/2022
   Councilmember Hampton expressed appreciation and gratitude
  to President Pomeroy and Member Phelps for their service on
  the PUSD Board of Education.

ADJOURNMENT  On the order of the President and Mayor, the special joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Board of Education
  adjourned at 6:29 p.m.

  Vic M. Gordo, May
  City of Pasadena

Council Minutes  6  03/07/2022
